interface.name: banner_desktop_v1
interface.description: Each Wine process is a separate Wayland client, so a Windows virtual desktop can't be built from subsurfaces. Instead the process that owns the desktop window marks one surface as the desktop, and every process reports where its top-level windows sit on that desktop and the global window stacking order. The compositor draws the desktop at the bottom, the windows at the reported positions, and sends pointer and keyboard input to the desktop surface; Wine routes it to the right window.

request.name: set_desktop

description.summary: mark a surface as the virtual desktop

request.description: The surface is drawn at the origin, below every window, and sets the size of the desktop.

request.name: set_window

description.summary: place a top-level window on the desktop

request.description: Position of the top-left corner of the surface in desktop coordinates, and the window handle used by set_zorder.

request.name: set_zorder

description.summary: report the desktop's window stacking order

request.description: Visible top-level window handles as 32-bit values, topmost first.
